(1) 321,910 estimated new US female breast cancers in 2026 (SEER Cancer Stat Facts, Female Breast Cancer). (2) 0.91 not metastatic at diagnosis: SEER's stage distribution on the same page, localized 64% and regional 27% against distant 6% and unstaged 2% (SEER 21 excluding Illinois, 2016 to 2022). (3) 0.727 HR-positive HER2-negative: of case patients with known HR/HER2 status 36,810 of 50,571, 72.7%, were HR(+)/HER2(-) (Howlader N, Altekruse SF, Li CI, Chen VW, Clarke CA, Ries LA, Cronin KA, 'US incidence of breast cancer subtypes defined by joint hormone receptor and HER2 status', J Natl Cancer Inst 2014;106(5):dju055, doi 10.1093/jnci/dju055, PMID 24777111). (4) 0.267 meeting a published high-risk adjuvant definition: 519 of 1,947 patients with stage I-III HR-positive invasive breast cancer met the MonarchE criteria (Wu J, Zhao Z, Li M, Cao J, Zhang K, 'Eligibility for adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitors in HR+/HER2- early breast cancer: insights from a large cohort in central south China', Transl Breast Cancer Res 2026;7:1, doi 10.21037/tbcr-25-27), 26.7%. (5) 0.68 still on adjuvant endocrine therapy, which the study requires: 'By 4.5 years, 32% discontinued therapy' among 8,769 Kaiser Permanente Northern California patients with hormone-sensitive stage I-III disease (Hershman DL, Kushi LH, Shao T, Buono D, Kershenbaum A, Tsai WY, Neugut AI, 'Early discontinuation and nonadherence to adjuvant hormonal therapy in a cohort of 8,769 early-stage breast cancer patients', J Clin Oncol 2010;28(27):4120-4128, doi 10.1200/JCO.2009.25.9655, PMID 20585090). (6) x3, the eligibility window: EMBER-4 admits patients between 24 and 60 months into adjuvant endocrine therapy (NCT05514054), a 36-month window, so three annual cohorts stand inside it at any time. 321,910 x 0.91 x 0.727 x 0.267 x 0.68 x 3 = 115,998 patients, and 115,998 / 160,000 = 0.724990
column12: the number to argue with is (4). Lilly publishes no definition of 'increased risk of disease recurrence based on clinical-pathological risk features', so the MonarchE share stands in for it, and the published proxies spread wide: 26.7% on MonarchE criteria in the Chinese cohort cited, against 36.2% MonarchE and 59.0% NATALEE among 334 HR-positive HER2-negative stage I-III patients at a Colombian centre (Golemba AS et al., Cureus 2026;18(1):e101836, doi 10.7759/cureus.101836). EMBER-4's 8,000 patients suggest a definition nearer NATALEE's than MonarchE's, so this row most likely errs low, perhaps by half. column12: THE ROW TO ARGUE WITH, AND FOR THIS LAYER IT ERRS HIGH BY A LONG WAY. EMBER-3's 5.6 months is monotherapy in ESR1-mutated advanced or metastatic disease, where treatment runs until progression and progression comes quickly. EMBER-4, the gate this layer is built on, is ADJUVANT: NCT05514054 randomises patients with resected early breast cancer who have already had 2 to 5 years of adjuvant endocrine therapy, and adjuvant endocrine therapy is given for years by design, not until progression. A 77% annual stopping rate is the metastatic business, not the adjuvant one. Two things to set against it. The label's own combination figure is longer, 'the median duration of exposure was 7.7 months (range 1 day to 25.3 months)' with abemaciclib, which would give 0.657. And nothing measured exists for adjuvant imlunestrant, because the readout has not happened. I wrote the approved product's rate because discontinuation_pct is an asset-level key and the asset's business today is metastatic; a reviewer building the adjuvant layer should consider carrying a layer-level override, and lly_inluriyo.csv's Breast Neoplasms rows are where it would go
